source: scripts/sync_mapper.py (this skill is the sole maintainer since 2026-09-11; the vault-side generate_map.py is retired)
changes: annotation and wikilink masking including multiline notes
explicit Markdown input filenames
expected physical pages for coverage auditing
para_blocks fallback for middle JSON
page range offsets for multi-volume files (--page-range-offset)
catalog rebuild records only a vault-relative config path (--rebuild-config); no machine paths
merged bodies: chapter headings take their first printed page from frontmatter chapter_metadata

chapter_metadata is read by YAML indentation: nested lists are not new entries, flow sequences (pages: [61, 80]) are understood, one quote pair is stripped, and a repeated title keeps the first entry's page
headings and frontmatter titles share one normalization, and a heading title is taken from the block's first line only
parse_offset_config is shared with pdf_sync so a dry run cannot disagree with the real run; incomplete page range offsets raise one friendly message
catalog entries merge with the previous record (fields a run does not supply are kept) and are written atomically via os.replace
--pages removed from the mapper CLI: only --rerun-pages remains, and it forces a cache refresh without limiting the run

line recovery is det-v2: the crop bleeds about half a block height of white space on every side before detection (a one-line footnote cropped tight is an unreadable 25px strip), boxes centred outside the original block are dropped, and boxes sharing a text row are merged so the footnote marker joins its sentence instead of standing as its own line

detection that covers less than half the block by height OR by area is treated as a miss - a lone circled marker spans the full height on a twentieth of the width - and falls back: a block no taller than 1.6 body line heights (0.025 normalized where the page has no line boxes at all) is read whole, a taller one is cut by horizontal projection whose row gap calibrates on the block's own bands, so a text block can never end up with no line box

the detection cache key carries the algorithm version (LINE_DETECTION_ALGORITHM), so a recipe change retires the results of the previous one while the pNNNN.json recognition caches keep their append path

line-less text blocks (page_footnote above all, plus index/ref_text/image_caption/image_footnote/aside_text) get their line boxes from PP-OCRv5_mobile_det detection run on the block crop only; running heads, page numbers, footers, tables and formulas are deliberately excluded so alignment gets no text the Markdown lacks
the OCR cache filename carries a short hash of the page's whole line set (p0024-<hash8>.json), so a page whose line set grew can no longer hide behind an old cache file

a pre-supplement p0024.json cache is reused instead of discarded: only the supplementary lines are recognized and their characters are appended after the cached ones, which holds because those lines are read last
detected line boxes are cached under lines/p0024-<blockhash>.json, so a repeat run needs neither a page render nor the detection model

character boxes are scaled from the CTC column numbers themselves ([first-half a step, last+half a step] stretched over MinerU's line box) instead of word_info[0]: PaddleX sorts the batch by aspect ratio when it computes the valid column count but writes it back in the original order, so every line was given another line's ratio - a long line came out as only its first few characters (the rest collapsed to zero width and were dropped) and a short line was squeezed into the start of its own line box

an Obsidian block identifier at the end of a line (## 注释 ^tb-c01-h0053) is masked out of the visible text and out of the normalized heading title: it is a link target, not print, and it used to cost every such heading thirteen characters of coverage

page characters are re-ordered into layout reading order before alignment: inside a horizontal band whose lines split into disjoint columns the left column is read first, so a hanging sub-heading (title on the left half, body text set beside it on the same lines) no longer interleaves with that body text and stops being dropped by the monotonic alignment; bands and within-column order are untouched

a second recognition backend runs the same PP-OCRv5 weights on ONNX Runtime (--ocr-backend onnx, --onnx-model, --onnx-device cpu|dml|auto, --onnx-device-id, batched with --rec-batch-size): both backends share one cropping routine and one chars_from_columns, so a line yields identical text and identical boxes - 683 lines over physical pages 41-60 of world-ancient-lower compared line by line came out equal with a maximum coordinate difference of 0 on CPU and on DirectML; only speed differs (20 pages: paddle CPU 81.8s, onnx CPU 88.5s, onnx DirectML 10.3s on a Radeon RX 9070 GRE)

DirectML adapter selection enumerates DXGI and takes the adapter with the most dedicated video memory instead of DirectML's default device 0, which is commonly the integrated GPU and an order of magnitude slower; auto falls back to CPU when no discrete adapter is found, and the provider and adapter name are printed on the mapper's closing line

the OCR cache is separated per backend: load_or_run_ocr honours an engine-supplied cache_scope (onnx-<model>-<provider>-b<batch>) and pdf_sync folds the backend name, the ONNX model file hash, the resolved provider, the adapter index and the batch size into the cache identity

line recovery now also runs for the ONNX backend: its detection model is PaddleOCR's either way, so a footnote or a table of contents keeps its recovered line boxes; Tesseract and Kraken still skip it to stay installable without PaddlePaddle

dot leaders are collapsed before alignment: a run of two or more dot characters (. and the middle-dot family) becomes one unit on both sides, because Markdown writes two ellipses that NFKC expands into six periods while the page carries dozens of printed dots, and the surplus used to push the page number after them out of the alignment window; a single middle dot is left alone since it is a real separator in Chinese titles, and the collapsed unit carries every source character in the run so each one still receives the leader's bounding box

the ONNX recognition backend defaults to PP-OCRv6_medium_rec and reads its character dictionary AND its input geometry from the model directory's inference.yml (PostProcess.character_dict plus PreProcess RecResizeImg.image_shape) instead of assuming PP-OCRv5's 3x48x320, with the yml checked against the static dimensions the ONNX graph declares so a mismatched pair of files fails loudly instead of silently rescaling every line; the Paddle backend still defaults to PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec because that is the only Paddle-format weight kept on disk for the fallback path. Measured on world-ancient-lower physical pages 41-60 (658 lines, batch 16, DirectML on an RX 9070 GRE, two runs, faster kept): character accuracy 99.64% -> 99.85% and 11.24s -> 13.83s for the 20 pages; DirectML and CPU agree line for line (658/658) on v6, and DirectML takes 186 of the graph's 188 nodes

per-character recognition confidence: the ONNX CTC decode also returns, for each character, the highest softmax value over the columns it occupies (PaddleX's line rec_score averages the same per-character maxima); scores ride in the OCR cache as an optional third item (old two-item entries still load, with no score), are attached to mapped characters on alignment, and are written to the chapter sidecar only below SCORE_CEILING (0.98) as chars[].score, plus candidates[].score for the OCR reading of a disagreeing character; a chapter carries scoreCeiling only when its run produced scores, and index chapters gain scoredCharacters. The plugin's backflow marker %%ha-bf:id%% is masked like annotation notes

book-folder layout: every path the mapper writes (index chapter keys, map files, page summaries, the PDF, the index location, the rebuild config) is relative to the book folder (--markdown-root), and the book entry is written to <book>/_数据/book.json instead of a shared catalog.json beside the output; the PDF and the output must lie inside the book folder, so the folder can be renamed, moved or handed to someone else as is

not print, so not counted: presentational HTML tags (<small>, <sup>, <sub> ...) and a generated '## 注释' / '## 注' heading that is directly followed by footnote definitions; a real section called 注释 stays text
alignment folds 〇 ○ O o 0 into one unit on both sides, so a 〇 the recognizer read as the letter O still gets its box; the Markdown character is what is written

line recovery is det-v5: a running head (header/doc_title) is read when its text is one of the page's Markdown headings (chapter titles printed in a banner); a block keeps being searched for line-high strips no line box covers (edge strip >= 0.8, inner strip >= 1.8 of the block's own line height) and ink rows found there by projection become lines; lines detected in a line-less block grow outwards along connected ink until a blank run wider than one line height, never shrinking (an inward re-measure once cut every footnote's closing 。); line boxes taller than 1.8x the page median and wider than 3x their height are split by detection with height-aware row merging (a drop cap stays its own box), falling back to projection, cached as lines/pNNNN-split-<hash>.json
ink_levels: a strip that is almost all paper (a three-character last line) takes its ink level from the darkest pixel when that pixel is clearly dark, instead of calling the strip blank

gap repair after alignment: a run of up to four unplaced characters (no candidate) between two placed neighbours on one printed row of one block is re-read on the neighbour-to-neighbour crop and accepted only if it spells neighbours plus gap exactly; failing that the ONNX backend runs CTC forced alignment (Viterbi over the crop's column probabilities) and accepts it only if both neighbours land back in their own boxes and every gap character scores >= FORCED_MIN_SCORE (0.001) - measured on 120 gaps of 儒学、数术与政治: real characters median 0.06, a substituted absent character at most 3e-5; the score is written as chars[].score; --no-gap-repair turns it off; the closing line reports gapReread and gapForced

reports separate characters with a candidate (position known, reading in doubt) from those with no box at all: index chapters gain unlocatedCharacters, the coverage report prints both, delivery-report gains unlocatedCharacters/unlocatedCharacterRanges and additionalRepair pages count only the unlocated ones; missing[] keeps its meaning for the plugin

measured on 儒学、数术与政治 (339 pages, DirectML): characters with no box 543 -> 158, placed characters 298152 -> 298557, 63 characters on four merged double lines moved from wrong two-line boxes to their own line (checked against the page image), 3 lost; whole run 236 s

book glyph table (--variant-equivalent 黄黃, config variantEquivalents): groups of verified variants, printed form first, are folded into one unit on both sides of the alignment, so a book kept in its printed glyphs (黄 説 爲) still takes the boxes of what the recognizer reads (黃 說 為) instead of flagging every one as a disagreement; the Markdown character is what is written; one character per group, checked by pdf_sync; empty by default

estimated boxes for punctuation the recognizer skipped: after alignment and gap repair, a run of ESTIMATABLE_CHARS with no box and no candidate gets a box from its nearest placed neighbours in the same block along the writing direction (vertical-rl: down the column) - between two neighbours on one line it is laid out from the first at half a pitch per mark, compressed but never stretched; otherwise it follows the previous character (a vertical mark sits in the half cell below it) or precedes the next; unread hanzi are never guessed. Boxes go to blocks[].estimated [{from,to,page,rect}] only - not chars, still listed in missing - so the plugin keeps locating by read positions alone; index chapters gain estimatedCharacters, the coverage report says how many unlocated characters have one; --no-estimate turns it off. Measured on the 黄道周集 vertical trial (4 pages): 144 of 145 unread marks estimated

supplementary model parts: blocks MinerU lost entirely (a byline filed as a page number, two page footnotes on 黄道周集 p.17) can be added as an extra modelParts entry holding just those pages' blocks and ocr_text column boxes (from PaddleOCR-VL block boxes cut into columns by ink projection); parts merge per page, so the mapper recognizes those lines like any other. With the glyph table and this supplement the 4-page trial went from 73.0% to 91.3% character coverage and passed block acceptance

vertical line recovery: with --writing-mode vertical-rl the whole row-based recovery (row merging, coverage, projection fallback, ink widening, hole strips, tall-line splitting) runs in transposed space - page image and every box swap x and y, so a column becomes a row - and the detector still sees upright crops through TransposedDetector, its polygons swapped back; before this, side-by-side vertical columns overlap completely in y and merge_row_boxes folded a two-column footnote into one box. Cached line files for vertical pages hold transposed boxes under transposed-rect digests, so they never collide with horizontal ones
compatibility: MinerU PDF Sync sidecar schema version 1
maintenance: Bundled snapshot. Update deliberately with mapper tests and sidecar compatibility checks; never overwrite a local plugin automatically.
